rounds.text: Naksh Precious Metals Ltd is heavily discounted by the market, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.64x against a book value of ₹ 5.76 per share [E1]. This deep discount is further emphasized by the provider's key ratios showing a P/B of 0.62x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.83x [E6]. Beneath the depressed share price sitting at only 13% of its 52-week range [E4], the business is undergoing a dramatic fundamental turnaround characterized by explosive top-line acceleration. Compounded sales growth over the last 3 years has surged to 153% [E14], backed directly by scanX signal engine screens highlighting a massive 750% year-over-year sales increase [E51] and strong overall sales growth [E52]. This operational momentum has already begun flowing to the bottom line, evidenced by a positive compounded profit growth of 7% over 5 years [E15]. Conceded: [E3], [E7], [E8], [E12], [E13], [E16], [E17], [E18], [E19], [E54].

Naksh Precious Metals Ltd carries severe structural risks and negative profitability metrics that render its low asset valuation entirely justified [E7, E8]. The company destroys shareholder value over multiple timeframes, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded share price growth of -14%, a 5-year decline of -32%, a 3-year drop of -41%, and a 1-year collapse of -42% [E16, E17, E18, E19]. Operational efficiency is deeply compromised, evidenced by a return on assets of -7.54% and a return on equity of -6.17%, both lagging drastically behind sector benchmarks [E7, E8]. Long-term top-line erosion is pronounced, with compounded sales shrinking by -28% over 10 years and -24% over 5 years, accompanied by decelerating earnings growth [E12, E13, E54]. The company also fails to return capital to investors, offering a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E14, E51, E52].

The bear relies heavily on long-term historical decay, but ignores the sharp, explosive inflection in recent fundamental performance [E12, E13]. The business is undergoing a massive operational turnaround, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 153% over the last 3 years and an extraordinary year-over-year sales surge of 750% [E14, E51, E52]. While past share prices and long-term top-line metrics reflect historical struggles, punishing the stock at 0.64x book value and 0.62x against a sector benchmark of 2.83x completely overlooks this sudden and powerful revenue velocity [E1, E6, E12, E13, E16, E17]. Conceded: [E3, E7, E8, E18, E19, E54].

The bull points to a three-year compounded sales growth of 153% and a year-over-year surge of 750% as proof of an operational turnaround, but this short-term top-line velocity sits against a decadelong structural decay where 10-year sales shrank by 28% and 5-year sales shrank by 24% [E12, E13, E14, E51, E52]. Conceded: [E14, E51, E52]. Furthermore, this recent revenue expansion fails to generate shareholder returns, as evidenced by a negative return on equity of -6.17% and a negative return on assets of -7.54% against healthy sector benchmarks of 11.41% and 6.17%, proving that the surge lacks profitable conversion [E7, E8]. The bull's dismissal of long-term history is contradicted by continuous wealth destruction, shown by compounded share price contractions of 14% over 10 years, 32% over 5 years, 41% over 3 years, and 42% over 1 year [E16, E17, E18, E19].
